channel.title: Latest alerts from washingtonpost.com
channel.description: An unofficial feed created by Derek Willis.

item.title: Justice Department investigating five TV networks over White House pool coverage
item.description: The agency said the probe seeks to determine whether Fox News, CNN, ABC, CBS and NBC violated antitrust laws. It marks a sharp escalation in the Trump administration’s use of its powers against perceived enemies in the press.

item.title: Trump can’t stop talking about vomit and Texas barbecue
item.description: Republicans need President Donald Trump to use his swagger to hype up embattled U.S. Senate candidate Ken Paxton. He keeps talking about barf.

item.title: 8 killed, including 2 young children and a pregnant woman, in shooting in Erie, Pennsylvania, authorities say
item.description: Erie police said seven of the victims were family members and related to the shooter, who appeared to have died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

item.title: At least 12 killed and hundreds injured in attack at Saudi Arabia’s international airport in Riyadh, authorities say
item.description: Amid the wider Iran war, Yemen’s Houthis are striking Saudi oil infrastructure, as compounding Middle East conflicts threaten to expand. The rebel group did not immediately claim responsibility for the attack, which authorities said killed one American.

item.title: The new welfare queen is Brad. Right-wing pundits are furious.

item.title: Montana Democrat who refuses to drop out may spoil party’s Senate hopes
item.description: Candidate Alani Bankhead vigorously denies claims she is a Republican plant running to take votes away from a more popular independent.

item.title: Death toll rises to 4 after Hurricane Isaias roared ashore near Destin, Florida, and swept inland
item.description: Ferocious winds were also driving power outages across Florida, Alabama and Georgia as of early Saturday.

item.title: The dads who are speaking up about the Cornell rape allegations
item.description: On social media, fathers are modeling age-appropriate conversations they’re having with their kids about consent.

item.title: Pentagon raises official toll of troops who died during war with Iran to 21
item.description: The Post exclusively reported last month that the numbers of service members lost was greater than what the Pentagon was reporting in its public database.

item.title: Christa Pike discharged from hospital, 10 days after failed execution attempt in Tennessee
item.description: Pike has moved to a rehabilitation center, according to her attorneys and the Tennessee Department of Correction.

item.title: Carolyn Hax: Compartmentalizing wife’s habitual cheating. Strategy or insanity?
item.description: Letter writer exists around wife’s serial infidelity by pretending it’s not there, and asks, “Am I just a masochistic time bomb”?

item.title: Trump showers voters with checks and tax relief in final sprint to midterms
item.description: From diesel tax breaks to direct checks, the president is attempting to break through to economically anxious voters.

item.title: Hundreds of thousands without power across Florida, Alabama, Georgia after Isaias makes landfall
item.description: Storm surge warnings have ended after Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, but flash flooding risks remain as the storm moves across Alabama.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias makes landfall in Florida as a high-end Category 2 storm
item.description: Isaias struck late Friday near Destin, as the National Hurricane Center warned of “life threatening storm surge” that was already affecting the Gulf Coast. The storm had strengthened early Friday to a Category 3 before downgrading slightly to a Category 2, with maximum sustained winds at 105 mph at the time its eye crossed the shore.

item.title: More than 500 trees eyed for removal from East Potomac Golf Links, the D.C. course Trump is seeking to redesign
item.description: The first phase begins Saturday and contains 169 trees marked for removal, according to a federal court filing. A second phase covering 90 trees would follow, and the National Park Service says as many as 529 could eventually come down. The disclosure was part of the government’s response to an expanded lawsuit challenging President Donald Trump’s proposed transformation of the century-old facility.

item.title: 10 Costco purchases chefs swear by
item.description: When it comes to cooking at home, culinarians like the rotisserie chicken, frozen vegetables, Parmigiano-Reggiano and more.

item.title: The U.S. can’t win in Iran until Trump makes a decision, Fareed Zakaria writes
item.description: To get out of this quagmire, Washington must determine what it wants.

item.title: Trump says Russia has agreed to supply diesel fuel to the global marketplace in bid to lower prices
item.description: The amount is small compared with U.S. demand, but the deal aligns the U.S. with Russia and against Ukraine’s efforts to bomb Russian refineries.

item.title: FlyDubai co-pilot planned 9/11-style attack on Israel’s main airport, UAE says
item.description: Hamam al-Hammami, a 29-year-old Omani national, intended to cause “the greatest possible number of human casualties,” the Emirati attorney general said.

item.title: Conservative commentator Katie Zacharia chosen as new White House press secretary, according to administration officials
item.description: Zacharia replaces Karoline Leavitt, who departed the White House in August after giving birth to her second child.

item.title: Vance says he's skeptical Fort Hood shooter’s execution will actually be live-streamed and won't watch if it is
item.description: The vice president’s comments mark the first time a top Trump official has signaled some unease with the Pentagon’s decision to make the execution public.

item.title: Mike Ditka, legendary Chicago Bears coach, dies at 86
item.description: He helped revolutionize the tight end position, but it was as a coach that he built his legacy, leading the 1985 Bears to the franchise’s only Super Bowl victory.

item.title: Democrats can ask and ask. I won’t drop out of Montana’s Senate race.
item.description: The political establishment is trying to override the voters.

item.title: Trump escalates effort to fire Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook after Supreme Court setback
item.description: A commission that will report to the president will assess the mortgage fraud allegations against her and consider evidence from a closed-door hearing at the White House next month.

item.title: ICE didn’t know 5-year-old boy was in car when officer fired on Dominican man in New York, Homeland Security secretary says
item.description: Federal authorities said Oscar Belgal, 28, used his car to ram government vehicles and endanger officers on Thursday. New York officials, including Gov. Kathy Hochul and New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, have denounced the agency and demanded that ICE pause enforcement operations in the state.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias intensifies to Category 3 as it approaches the Florida Panhandle. These cities could face the worst impacts.
item.description: The storm is expected to make landfall Friday evening. The Florida Panhandle, eastern Alabama, large parts of Georgia and portions of South Carolina face a threat for destructive winds and tornadoes.

item.title: Nobel prize. Execution live stream. Senate debates. ICE shooting. Hurricane. Doomsday bunkers. Costco must-buys. Catch up now.
item.description: Today’s seven most important and interesting stories.

item.title: Navanethem ‘Navi’ Pillay, South African jurist, awarded Nobel Peace Prize
item.description: The Nobel committee recognized the jurist and former U.N. human rights chief for her work helping “to strengthen the institutions of international law.”

item.title: ICE officer fired at least seven rounds in shooting that wounded a man in a car on a crowded city street, New York officials say
item.description: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said a 5-year-old child was in the car at the time of the shooting. The Department of Homeland Security said an immigration officer fired his weapon during a “targeted enforcement operation” while attempting to apprehend an undocumented Dominican man with a criminal history.

item.title: Virginia county sues to block President Donald Trump from building his 250-foot-tall triumphal arch
item.description: Arlington County’s all-Democratic board argues in a lawsuit filed in federal court in Virginia that the Trump administration failed to adequately evaluate potential environmental impacts of the project as required by federal law. The administration plans to build the arch on an island in the Potomac River that is officially part of D.C. but is within a few hundred yards of Arlington, a county of about 240,000 people that is home to several federal agencies.

item.title: At 81, he’s the most-cited nutrition expert. Here’s what he eats in a day.
item.description: Walter Willett’s research has changed the way Americans eat, revealing how diet and other lifestyle choices can shape your risk of chronic illnesses.

item.title: Fort Hood shooter’s execution by firing squad will be livestreamed, Defense Department says
item.description: The announcement came after earlier comments Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made indicating he wanted the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan to be public. Hasan is a former U.S. Army psychiatrist who opened fire on dozens of people at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009, killing 13 people and injuring 32 others.

item.title: Why are fewer teens identifying as gay or bisexual? Researchers aren’t sure.
item.description: The decline is particularly striking among ninth-grade girls, according to Jean Twenge, a professor of psychology at San Diego State University, who analyzed Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data.

item.title: Trump officials block Microsoft’s access to program for employee green cards
item.description: Vice President JD Vance announced the suspension, saying it would affect H-1B visas and aims to protect U.S. workers.

item.title: U.S. officials charge Maduro, wife with torturing dissidents
item.description: The Justice Department filed a new indictment against deposed Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife, who have been in federal prison since January.

item.title: Search warrants against the former prince Andrew were unlawful, court finds, but misconduct investigation may continue
item.description: British police acknowledged applying for the warrants under the wrong statutory provision, the judge said. King Charles III’s brother was taken into custody in February over suspicions of misconduct in public office connected to his relationship with the convicted child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Army report cites systemic flaws that led to Black Hawk helicopter’s fatal 2025 collision with airliner in D.C.
item.description: The documents, reviewed by The Post ahead of public dissemination, detail numerous shortfalls in Army procedures and policy that investigators said contributed to the tragedy, which killed 67 people.

item.title: Sens. Merkley and Daines: Our bipartisan plan would reform the U.S. Senate
item.description: For too long, both parties have been hamstrung by the Senate’s tangled rules.

item.description: The university’s campus police alert said that Dilan Shaan Ashar has been reunited with family. The alert did not specify where or when the 22-year-old was found. Earlier this week, family members released an emotional plea to the public that spread across social media feeds throughout the D.C. region.
